items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Ray Conniff; the name is introduced solely by the interviewer.

ctx.x: I went to Florida once and I was jamming with Jack Petersen, a great guitar player down there. And he’d say, “What do you want to play?” And I said, “I want to play “Chicken a la Swing,” and he knew the first part. And I said how many guys are jamming “Chicken a la Swing?” Everybody else would call like “Monk’s Mood.” No we were playing “Chicken a la Swing.” So there was all this guitar stuff going on, and that’s how the guitar all started.
I mean I was hearing Ray Conniff when I grew up. Wow.

It was fun. I think, and then I started to play, I met a kid at this day camp I was working at. Because the only other job I ever had was a day camp counselor. And I like working with kids and I had a lot of fun doing it. And I had been there as a camper and I just stayed there and made a little money in the summer. And there was a guy there who studied with Barry Galbraith, who is a great guitar player, played rhythm guitar on every record you would own. He’s on Clifford Brown Strings and he’s on all the Tony…
